_comment: v8 (L41): defaultMode=bypassPermissions — the steward session is prompt-free by default; no launch flag to remember. v7 (L40): THE USER BOUNDARY IS THE SECURITY BOUNDARY. Everything inside math-lsp is expendable by xor's declaration — no in-session structural denial exists; run with any permission mode, --dangerously-skip-permissions included. The allow list below only smooths default-mode sessions. What escapes the user keeps its guards elsewhere: origin/main (server-side, Box-2 promote) and spend (the breaker's uid-forgery-proof override lane). Lane discipline (steward never hand-edits member source or pushes) is doctrinal, for record-truth — detected via git history + owner-records, not prevented.
_comment_deny: The operator denylist lives at ~/.config/publication-denylist, outside every repository, because a list that IS the disclosure is safest when it is simply not present in the tree. Only the secret paths themselves are denied. proj/ and other gitignored directories are DEV WORKSPACE and are deliberately NOT denied: an earlier revision blocked Read(./proj/**) and that is a control with no path through (L48) — it stopped ordinary work on drafts and the firings ledger while protecting nothing that was still there. Omission from the seal, from git, from Serena's index and from publication-check's walk is about scope, not secrecy, and none of those should imply the agent may not read.
